citations.quote: The truth is equally well-defined: the truth is that markets are efficiently inefficient.
Capacity is the investment amount beyond which returns will be negatively affected by new investments.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Efficiently Inefficient Markets: framing the Pedersen "efficiently inefficient" view of markets — why prices are nearly but not exactly efficient, why active managers can earn returns above the market in equilibrium, and how anomalies fit as compensation for risk-bearing capacity rather than as mispricings to be arbitraged away
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Efficiently Inefficient Markets
